I went back and forth on this one for a while. My experience was a pretty mixed bag, but I can see a lot of the charm and, frankly, the game is super cheap so I'm hesitant to be too critical. Since there's no "maybe" option for reviews though, I'll have to give it a "no" and do my best to explain why.

For the good:
I think the concept here is honestly really compelling!! It was interesting to explore the different levels, work to understand how you can put together your alibi as well as actually do the deed itself, and to uncover stories about all the characters along the way. This setup is pretty fun and especially for a point-and-click RPG Maker game I think it's done well, plus I did have a good time for my first few runs of each "level" (character + time period). Some of the endings were actually pretty creative too, especially in seeing how you'd have to set up your responses to other characters and use very specific timing to get some plans to go off without a hitch. I can respect just how many routes/endings there are, so it really does feel like you have a variety of ways to do everything, and the writing was pretty okay too. I feel like if you're not a chronic "must complete all achievements when possible before considering a game 'finished'" person like me, you'll prolly have a great time just exploring a few endings for each character and calling it a day.

For the bad:
Man, this game got to be a real slog when I tried to get every ending. There's quite a bit of dialogue, which is fun for the first lil while, but it *really* makes things drag when you've already read it all before but still have to go through the paces anyway or else risk ruining the ending you're going for. Additionally, picking some dialogue options but not others was the only way to achieve some endings ime. This made some runs a real exercise in patience once I had to keep retrying with subtly different dialogue choices, to the point where I might frankly recommend a guide if you want to get every ending also. This was such a bummer, since it did eventually ruin the premise that I originally enjoyed. Ultimately, I felt like seeing every ending was more of a "finish it just to have everything done" rather than a true attachment to the stories, which is ultimately why I decided to not recommend it since it just didn't hook me in the end.

All that being said, it's only 3 bucks and the initial "discovery" phase of playing through for the first handful of times was fairly enjoyable. Mostly up to you if you think it's worth your time =))

The Deed : Dynasty is a great follow up game to The Deed.  If you haven't played the Deed yet, I recommend you first start there yet it doesn't matter what order you play these games in. These games are great if you enjoy murder mystery kind of games.  

Although, What I like about Dynasty is that there are three different stories from three different time periods that you can invest your time in and try to get away with murder. The first game is short and only has one scenario, where as Dynasty has three scenarios. This in addition to plethora of murder weapons and items that you can pick up in order to do the murder is also great too and adds a lot of replay value. 

Keep in mind while playing this game, that it does matter how you talk to someone as well as what items you pick up and where you put them as well as what murder weapon you ultimately choose. When it comes to getting investigated every person in every scenario is heavily questioned and the whole house is searched. So, choices do ultimately matter in how the end result truly plays out! 

For example, in the first scenario in the Old English Castle, I tried to beat the man to death on the balcony and accidently fell to my death. In the second scenario in the Wild West Saloon, I murdered a man with a stripper's knife and tried to frame the dirty stripper as the killer but was caught in some lies by the dialogue system. These lies ended up coming back to bite me, when talking to the investigator as then I was seen as the main suspect! In which I wish I didn't lie as I could have gotten away with murder in this scenario because I had framed the stripper as the murderer pretty good! I was then sentenced to prison and died. 

Finally in the last scenario, I talked to everyone in the house and found out that one of my brothers had gotten mad and hit his wife who was also staying in the house weeks ago.  I found this out from my father in a dialog choice in which my father was happy that my brother had hit his wife. Then while I was investigating the house, I found a note that was written from my other brother that I was going to kill that was addressed to his sibling but didn't tell which sibling it was addressed to and talked about how he would not lend any money to that sibling. I then ended up talking to my brothers wife and found out that my brother has recently lost his job at the bank and it put some stress on their family. Knowing what I knew about my brother hitting his wife and losing his job, I framed my brother by leaving the note written by my other brother in his room with his wife and then I went and killed my other brother. However, before I killed my other brother. I took the corkscrew bottle opener from the cellar and used it as my murder weapon. I took this as the murder weapon because my brother liked to drink in the cellar and I figured after killing my brother and the investigator finding the note that the corkscrew would also make sense. Fast Forward to the investigation part, My brother was ultimately found guilty for killing of my brother and was executed. 

Overall I give the Deed Dynasty a 7/10! It is much better than the Deed because it has more scenarios as well as more murder weapons and ways to fully engage in the gameplay it presents.

As much as I love the idea of an inverted detective game, The Deed Dynasty just doesn't work. The collection of potential frameups consists of a single track per potential victim, and some fairly obvious logical leaps just don't get made (for some reason, framing the victim as a heretic in the witch hunting times scenario doesn't count as a motive for anyone who hates heretics, not even the person he explicit gave confessional).

What's more annoying, though, is that it's actually contemptuously easy to commit what is by any realistic definition a perfect crime - using poison guarantees leaving absolutely zero evidence trail - but unless you managed to get above a certain, rather arbitrary threshold for suspicion cast on someone else, the detective of the week will just magically know you did it and arrest you with no evidence. This never, ever stops being frustrating.
Good concept,  but clunky implementation.

[h1] What is this game? [/h1]
The Deed: Dynasty - is a reverse murder mystery game that follows 3 different members of the same family, murdering their "enemies" across different time periods. With the ultimate goal of avoiding getting caught for said murders.

[h2] Price/replay value [/h2]
Horrible - Bad - [u]Decent[/u] - Good - Amazing

[h2] Achievement hunting [/h2]
Mostly just doing the same murders with different scapegoats/weapons.
Overall not that difficult.

[h2] Pros/cons [/h2]
[b] Pros [/b]
[list]
[*]Nice settings 
[*]Large amount of dialogue options
[/list]

[b] Cons [/b]
[list]
[*]Incredibly repetitive
[*]No quick load option
[*]NPCs are very simple
[/list]

[h2] Overall opinion [/h2]
This game essentially plays like the first in the series, which isn't a good thing. 
The essential gameplay loop is selecting the same 5 dialogue options for every NPC (changing 1 if you need to frame someone else) and doing the same thing over and over with a mere difference of weapon and piece of evidence. The law enforcers will automatically arrest you, even if you are not suspicious...? Which feels incredibly one sided. Dialogue options purely serve to give you blackmail on certain characters. Which one gives said blackmail is a guessing game as you'll have to restart upon selecting the wrong one. 

Controls feel sluggish a lot of the time as there's no option to use wasd, which is weird for a 2016 game. Having enter/space and shift being your main dialogue controls is also weird in combination with the arrow keys. And the fact pressing F12 is supposed to reset, but actually just crashes the game is incredibly stupid. -- To add to this, there is an apparent lack of quick load, meaning you have to exit to the main menu to load a save. 

I enjoyed the first game in all its simplicity, the 2nd was well designed but the timer ruined it, and this one has none of the complexity of the 2nd, with the controls of the 1st. Though this game was a stepping stone, I really can't encourage doing more than a single run of these scenarios.

[h2] tldr; [/h2]
Repetitive, fairly bland. 

[h2] Should you buy it? [/h2]
I recommend against it unless you absolutely adore rpgmaker games.

《The Deed: Dynasty》作为《The Deed》的独立资料片，不仅延续了前作的精髓，更在剧情、玩法和体验上进行了全面的升级和扩展，为玩家带来了一场更为丰富和深刻的冒险之旅。游戏通过三段发生在不同时代的崭新剧情，深入探索了布鲁斯家族成员内心深处的卑鄙与秘密。这三个故事背景分别设定在15世纪的英格兰城堡、旧西部的边界小镇以及维多利亚时代的老庄园，为玩家提供了丰富多样的历史背景和环境设定。每个时代的故事都充满了悬疑与转折，让玩家在解谜的过程中不断感受到剧情的深度和吸引力。

游戏玩法依旧以文字冒险和益智解谜为主，但《The Deed: Dynasty》在策略性上进行了显著提升。玩家需要在游戏中做出正确的选择、放置合适的伪证，并巧妙地说服执法者，以逃脱法律的制裁。游戏中的每个决定都会对剧情走向和结局产生影响，这种高度的自由度和多样性让玩家每次游玩都能获得全新的体验。此外游戏还提供了多种犯罪手法和武器选择，玩家需要根据不同的情况选择合适的策略来达成目的。

角色塑造依然出色，每个角色都有其独特的性格和背景故事。玩家在与这些角色互动的过程中，不仅可以了解他们的内心世界，还能通过对话和选择影响游戏的进程和结局。游戏中还包含了许多不可操控的角色，其中一些甚至基于真实历史人物打造，这为游戏增添了更多的真实感和代入感。对话系统的改进也为玩家提供了更多的可控因素和分支选项，让每次游玩都充满惊喜。

尽管《Dynasty》在画面上可能不如一些大型游戏那样华丽，但其简洁明了的界面设计和符合时代背景的视觉效果却为游戏增色不少。游戏中的场景布置和角色形象都充满了历史气息，让玩家仿佛置身于真实的时代环境中。音效方面，游戏同样表现出色，背景音乐和角色配音都恰到好处地渲染了游戏的氛围和情感。

综上所述，《The Deed: Dynasty》是一款在剧情、玩法、角色和视听效果上都表现出色的冒险解谜游戏。它不仅延续了前作的优点，更在多个方面进行了创新和提升。对于喜欢犯罪题材、文字冒险和益智解谜的玩家来说无疑是一款不可错过的佳作。无论是沉浸在丰富的剧情中，还是享受解谜的乐趣和挑战策略性玩法，都能为你带来全新的游戏体验。

[h1]The Deed: Dynasty - Uma Trama de Vingança e Intriga ao Longo dos Séculos[/h1]

Introdução:
Em um enredo intricado onde o ódio e o desejo de vingança transcendem séculos, The Deed: Dynasty nos leva a uma jornada através do tempo, onde três membros de uma orgulhosa e nobre família estão unidos por um intento vingativo e homicida.

A Trama Sinistra:
Separados por cinco séculos, esses personagens compartilham uma única motivação: a necessidade de executar seus planos sombrios. Em um jogo de gato e rato, estratégias precisam ser traçadas, sangue precisa ser derramado e evidências precisam ser plantadas para que a verdade seja obscurecida.

Os Protagonistas da Tragédia:
Cada membro da família carrega consigo suas próprias motivações e segredos sombrios. Desde o nobre patriarca até o jovem herdeiro sedento por poder, cada um desempenha um papel crucial nessa dança mortal, onde a linha entre vítima e assassino se torna turva.

O Jogo da Morte:
The Deed: Dynasty não é apenas um jogo de estratégia; é um mergulho profundo na mente dos conspiradores, onde cada escolha molda o destino dos personagens e o desenrolar da trama. Desde a meticulosa elaboração dos planos até a execução das ações mais cruéis, cada passo é calculado e cada consequência é imprevisível.

A Arte da Manipulação:
Em um mundo onde a verdade é apenas uma questão de perspectiva, a manipulação é a moeda mais valiosa. The Deed: Dynasty desafia os jogadores a explorarem as fraquezas de seus alvos, a semear a desconfiança entre aliados e a criar um emaranhado de mentiras e enganos para encobrir seus crimes.

Recomendação:
Para aqueles que buscam uma experiência intensa e cheia de reviravoltas, The Deed: Dynasty é uma escolha obrigatória. Sua narrativa envolvente, repleta de intrigas e traições, mantém os jogadores à beira de seus assentos, enquanto exploram as profundezas sombrias da alma humana. Prepare-se para mergulhar em um mundo de traições e segredos, onde a linha entre o bem e o mal é tênue e a verdade é tão volúvel quanto as sombras que a encobrem.

I am 32 years old.

My ex-wife and I have a daughter together, and we adopted our son together. Both are now 4 years old.

When we were going through our separation, I felt lost and unhappy. I was self-destructive. One day, I was so angry with everything spiraling out of control that I punched a concrete wall in a moment of overwhelming emotion. This resulted in breaking my fifth metacarpal in my right hand—the hand I worked with, played games with, and used to carry my children to bed—the hand I desperately needed to ensure I could continue providing.

Upon learning the severity of the self-inflicted damage, I became almost suicidal. Keep in mind that just a few months before this, I was the happiest man, with no history of depression or anxiety. I had never experienced anger outbursts, nor was I the type to break down and cry, but I was in a tough situation that truly prevented me from seeing the light on the other side.

With nothing better to do, I looked for a game I could play WITH ONE HAND while recovering. Somehow, I stumbled upon this game and read some of the comments. I decided it was worth a try... I must admit I didn't beat the game, nor did I play as much as some of you. In fact, I may have played this game for only a day or two. That being said, after doing so, I had a new joy and hope for life. I managed to leave behind the pain and suffering that had been thrust upon me. I could experience the joy and happiness of other people. I relaxed for 5 ♥♥♥♥ minutes listening to this music, long enough to realize that I would be okay.

After realizing this, I turned off the game and went back to work. My hand hurt a lot, but I was motivated. I stopped feeling so sorry for myself and became the father I needed to be at that moment, not the weak boy I was behaving like.

Today, I am close friends with the mother of my children. We don't fight, argue, or say hurtful things to each other. We are parents and friends.

Now I have 3 children. My third child is, wait, ALSO 4 YEARS OLD. The woman I am with was going through a very similar situation at the time of my separation, and we just unexpectedly stumbled into each other's lives. We have been dating for a year and are very happy together.

Moral of the story: you never know what life has in store for you, and if I had given up when all odds were against me, I wouldn't be where I am today. This silly little game helped me realize that.

Thank you.

RPG Maker strikes again!

The Deed: Dynasty is one of hundreds of low effort retro-pixel RPG Maker asset/construction kit flips spamming the Steam catalog, made with the RPG Maker video game construction kit... in their own words, "Our easy to use tools are simple enough for a child."  Like all RPG Maker "games", this is essentially a bunch of low quality/canned assets from RPG Maker coupled with a cringeworthy high school anime club fan fiction.

This RPG Maker asset flip is the third in a series of utter crap "adventure" games where the usual anime fantasy JRPG theme has been replaced with stock assets for a mansion as you plod through a craptastic murder mystery.  It's pure garbage. 

As with all RPG Maker games, the poor quality engine displays badly in fullscreen and doesn't have full HD support or any graphics tweaking options, making this unacceptable for any dedicated modern PC gamer.  The point can be made that the intention of RPG Maker is to make demos and small games to pass around friends, and shouldn't be used for "professional" game development.

Like most RPG Maker shovelware and asset flips, the game features extremely low quality copy + pasted 2D retro pixel art, looks awful, and has even worse gameplay.  RPG Maker is an absolutely terrible construction kit, and never results in games of any reasonable quality or value to gamers.

Notably the developer here couldn't work out how to use RPG Maker to make an RPG... and that's the only thing RPG Maker can do properly... except it's not even very good for making RPGs.  Instead, we have << ABOUT THE GAME >>

You don't have to take my word about how bad the game is, we can measure the interest in a game by how much people bothered to play it.  The Deed: Dynasty has achievements, and they show us a very clear picture that the game absolutely failed to capture any interest from gamers.  The most commonly and easily attained achievement is for finding the first guilty NPC, trivial to achieve, but less than 6 percent of players bothered to get that far before uninstalling the game.  That's a tiny, tiny proportion of gamers who even bothered with this.  Ouch.

Reviewing SteamDB to check how popular this game was with players reveals a surprise... there's a very healthy spike in player counts for the game.  But this isn't consistent with the achievement stats, that show less than 6 percent of players bothered playing the game for any reasonable amount of time.  How is it possible for this game to have so many concurrent players who didn't bother to played the game?  Trading cards.  People will use card idling software to collect the cards and sell them, but this won't trigger any achievements in-game.

That tells us people only really bought this game for trading cards, and that's a damning indictment of the woeful quality.  A closer look at the numbers shows the game just has a couple of players every week running up the game and idling it for cards, then deleting it.  We must ask how it benefits gamers for there to be so many games like this, with no merit as a serious game, that only generate sales from people idling and selling the trading cards.

The Deed: Dynasty is relatively cheap at $3 USD, but it's not worth it. Given the defects and quality issues with the game, coupled with the unrealistic price, this is impossible to recommend.  Gamers who want a good retro JRPG experience would be better off playing the originals, like Final Fantasy, Star Ocean or Chrono Trigger.
